title: Coverage Months a Ridgecrest Advantage Closing Settlement Still Charges For
content:
When a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment is settled on being brought to an end, the coverage months the settlement still charges for are found by setting what the plan premium charges standing on the account already cover against how long the enrollment has been in force.

The coverage months the plan premium charges standing on the account cover are counted as 3 for every such charge where the enrollment is billed quarterly, and as 1 for every such charge where the enrollment is billed monthly. The coverage months the enrollment has been in force are the whole months that have passed since the coverage effective date, and one more for the month in hand.

| Where those two counts stand | Coverage months the settlement still charges for |
| --- | --- |
| The enrollment is billed quarterly and the charges leave at least 3 coverage months the enrollment has been in force uncovered | 3 |
| The charges leave the enrollment covered for fewer coverage months than it has been in force, and either fewer than 3 are left uncovered or the enrollment is billed monthly | 1 |
| The charges cover every coverage month the enrollment has been in force | 0 |

No coverage month beginning after the coverage end date is ever charged into the closing settlement, because the coverage months the settlement still charges for are only ever coverage months the enrollment has already been in force for.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

*An enrollment billed quarterly, in force for 10 coverage months, with 2 plan premium charges standing on the account.* Those charges cover 6 coverage months, leaving 4 uncovered; the cadence is quarterly and at least 3 are uncovered, so the settlement still charges for 3.

*An enrollment billed quarterly, in force for 8 coverage months, with 2 plan premium charges standing on the account.* Those charges cover 6 coverage months, leaving 2 uncovered; fewer than 3 are uncovered, so the settlement still charges for 1.

*An enrollment billed monthly, in force for 5 coverage months, with 3 plan premium charges standing on the account.* Those charges cover 3 coverage months, leaving 2 uncovered; the cadence is monthly, so the settlement still charges for 1.

*An enrollment billed monthly, in force for 4 coverage months, with 4 plan premium charges standing on the account.* Those charges cover 4 coverage months, which is every coverage month the enrollment has been in force, so the settlement still charges for 0.
